T: Old trees, taller than anything in the Archive. The air smells of rain and pine.
F: A split-rail fence, grey with age. Someone mends it now and then.
S: A signpost. One arm reads ONWARD, pointing east. The other arm has been snapped off.
Behind the post, the trees don't quite meet.
c: A candle in an iron lantern, burning steadily at the roadside. It feels like the Archive's candles. Somehow, it feels safe.
J: A cocoon, half hidden in the long grass at the roadside.
The silk is thin here. Something inside is ticking, very softly, like a clock.
=: The great door of the Archive, set into a hill of old stone. From out here, it looks like it has always been part of the hill.
>: The road runs on east toward distant towers.
On the tallest one, something blinks red. Slowly. Like it's breathing.
H: The Waystation. Smoke curls from its chimney, and a painted sign over the door shows a running boot.
L: A strip of old leather, snagged on a low branch: a satchel strap, cracked with age.
Tucked behind it, a folded page in a careful, hurried hand:
"If I don't make it back, the letter still goes. A courier doesn't read the post. A courier delivers it."
<: The road runs west, toward the smell of turnips.

objects.name: Felix
lines: ...Ah. Awake. And a visitor! How delicious.
Five hundred years, by the look of the grass. Hm. I'd have wagered four. One does so hate to lose a wager.

answer: Felix Rook. Enchanté. I advised the last war.
Both sides, naturally. It lasted so much longer that way. Such drama. Such style.
Hmmmm. Now there is a question with a certain… je ne sais quoi.
Whatever causes the most fun, I think. A little rendezvous with someone important, perhaps.
Thank you for the door, my friend. I shall remember it. Probably.

questions.ask: You sound like a cheap stage villain.
answer: Cheap? Mon ami, I have never once in my life been cheap.
But a villain… magnifique. You do say the sweetest things.

farewell: Then I bid you adieu, my little door-opener.
Until we meet again. And we shall. I insist.

objects.name: Nib
lines: HALT! Nobody passes without a duel!
Ugh. Look at you. I'd beat you with a stick. I'd beat you with half a stick.
Go on, pass. I'm counting it as a win. That's forty-one.

answer: I'm Nib. What's it to ya?

questions.ask: What are you doing out here?

answer: Don't you have a job or something?

then: Nib bursts into tears and runs off down the road.

lines: They say you won in the Kingdom's pit. Three of the king's own.
Doesn't count. I had you first. Forty-one.
A brass plaque by the Waystation: REST HERE, COURIER. THE ROAD REMEMBERS EVERY RUNNER.
Under the words, a running boot, worn almost smooth by passing hands.
Half-buried in the grass: the signpost's missing arm. The paint reads ...ECREST.
Whatever it pointed to, it's pointing at the dirt now.
In the hollow of an old pine, out of the rain: a Heart Piece, wrapped in a courier's glove.
Wedged in the roots below the torn strap: a letter in oilcloth, dry after all this time.
The seal is unbroken. A courier doesn't read the post. You decide you won't either.
